bells.title: The school day
bells.hint: How many lessons the day holds, and when each of them runs.
bells.hintMore: The number of rows is the length of the school day: the week grid draws exactly this many. Only the last lesson is removed — a lesson number is what an hour is keyed by, and renumbering would rewrite the timetable already drawn. Times need not all be filled in: a row left empty shows in the grid as a number without a time, and moving a bell does not move the lessons. Shortening the day leaves the hours already scheduled where they are; new ones just cannot be put beyond it.
bells.busiest: Lessons are already scheduled up to number {{number}}: they stay in the grid, but no new ones can be put beyond the day.

studyDays.title: Study days of the week
studyDays.hint: Which weekdays the school teaches on.
studyDays.hintMore: A Saturday is a school day in plenty of schools. A weekday left unchecked is a day off for the whole school: the week grid locks it, copying a period skips it, and no lesson count includes it. Single days are marked up in the school year — a holiday, a break, a Saturday worked in lieu; here you set the week itself. The setting belongs to the year, so a school changing its week does so from the new year on and leaves last year's timetable as it was.
studyDays.noYear: The week belongs to a school year, and there is none yet — start one on the school year page.

teachers.detachKeeps: Their lessons and plans are kept; the assignments and the role are removed.

reference.presetHint: Or add them one at a time below. Names can be changed afterwards; «Grade 9» becomes «MYP 4» in one click.
reference.levelShort: The year of study is counted from the first year of school.
reference.levelExplain: The ordinal year counted from the first one, not the number inside the name. «MYP 4» is the ninth year of study, so its year is 9 — that is what every list sorts by.
reference.levelLocked: Courses use this year group, so its year of study is fixed — the sorting of every list depends on it. The name can still be changed.

reference.clearConfirm_other: Delete {{count}} year groups no course uses?

students.detachKeeps: Nothing is deleted: the person is taken off every course, and what they have done stays.

rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.hint: Where lessons take place. The list is yours; teachers choose from it.
rooms.hintMore: A room that already holds lessons cannot be deleted — «the lesson was in 214» stays true even after the room becomes a store cupboard. Archive it instead: it disappears from the timetable pickers and stays in the history. Mark a hall shared when several lessons at once are normal there: the timetable then keeps quiet about them instead of warning every single day.
rooms.empty: No rooms yet — lessons simply have none.

homegroups.title: Classes
homegroups.hint: Groups of students: 6A, 6B, DP1. Not the same thing as a year group.
homegroups.hintMore: A class is a set of students with a name, and nothing else. It holds no courses: which classes a course belongs to follows from who studies in it, so a written link would be a second answer to the same question — and «course 6A» with seven students from 6A and three from 6B is an ordinary state of affairs. Membership is set where the students are, in «School → Students»: a class is a property of a person. Knowing both — who is in a course and who is in a class — the timetable can finally warn that somebody is in two places at once.
homegroups.needYear: Add a school year first — a class belongs to one.

schools.title: Schools
schools.hint: Every school in this installation. Creating one and handing it its first administrator cannot be done from inside a school — that is what this section is for.
schools.invited: «{{email}}» is invited to {{name}} as an administrator — they will get in through Google on that address.

empty.title: No schools yet
empty.hint: Create the first one and invite its administrator: everything else — the calendar, the courses, the teachers — they set up themselves.

works.title: Assignments in this course
works.none: No assignments in this course yet.
works.windowHint: Answers can be sent only while the window is open.
works.windowHintMore: Before it opens the students do not see the work at all — there is no draft state here, the window is the decision about visibility. While it is open they solve and submit. Once it closes the work stays with them: the questions, their own answers, the marks and the conversation with you about a question are still there — only sending a new answer is no longer possible.
works.attemptsHint: The number is how many times a student may send an answer to one question.
works.attemptsHintMore: Set to 1 — the student submits once and cannot resubmit. Set to 3 — three submissions per question, and after the third the answer box closes. It is counted per question, not for the work as a whole, and an attempt is spent on every submission, whether you have checked it or not. Clear the box and they may submit as often as they like.
works.showResult: Show the verdict to the student straight away
works.showResultHint: The students see their marks as soon as you set them.
works.showResultHintMore: It all opens at once: the marks for each question, the final grade for the work and your comment. Switched off, the students see this after the window closes — a mark shown early travels round the class faster than your marking does.
works.impact: {{students}} students have already answered here: {{answers}} answers. Editing is allowed — they will see the change immediately.
works.deleteWithTasks: Delete «{{name}}» with its {{count}} questions? The answers of the students go with it.

Paste a screenshot straight into the text with Ctrl+V; anything else — a pdf with the questions, a sheet to print — goes below as a file.

works.dropHere: Drop files here, or click to choose

works.showToClass: Show to the class: the file appears with the assignment for students and parents

works.attachHiddenOff: Files attached now are seen by the class — students and parents. Question papers, the blank, a worked solution after the lesson.

works.homeworkHint: Where the work is shown in the lesson, not what kind it is: a test set for home is still a test.

scan.readingHint: The browser straightens each header and sends only that strip — not the whole sheet.
scan.readingAndSorting: What has been read is already here: start sorting it out, no need to wait for the end of the pile. The rest of the pages will turn up on their own.
scan.stillReading: The pile is still being read. Move on once all of it is: half a pile must not be recorded.
scan.flipWhileReading: No turning while the reading runs: the page would be re-read against the request already in flight.
scan.checkHint: Everything below is what will be written. Look it over, or trust it and write.
scan.applyNeedsFile: Point at the PDF and write it all down

trouble.first_name_only: signed with a first name only
trouble.placed_by_guess: placed by a guess, not by a name

scan.questionsHint: How many questions were in this work, and what is the top mark for one? The blank always has fifteen cells; the extra ones must stay empty — that is how a shifted reading gets caught.
scan.perQuestionHint: The top box is what the question is called, the bottom one is its top mark. Leave the name empty and the question is called by its place in the list.
scan.printBlankHint: — blank sheets are printed in advance, a year's worth at a time.

about.pileOrder: The works follow one another in any order — there is no need to sort them alphabetically.
about.pileSheets: A work may run to any number of sheets: one, two, eight. There is no «two each» rule.
about.pileConditions: Question papers may go before every work, once at the top of the pile, or not at all. The first way is the most reliable: it marks the boundaries between works without any reading.
about.limitsOneWork: One pile, one assignment. The blank carries neither a name nor an assignment number, so a sheet from another test cannot be told from one of yours.
about.limitsHeader: The name has to be written by hand in the header of the blank: that is how a sheet finds its owner.
about.limitsCells: Marks belong in the cells of the blank. A mark in a cell this work does not have counts as a shifted reading, and you will be asked about it.
about.afterStrip: Only the header is read — the strip with the name and the mark cells. Solutions and rough work never leave your machine.
about.afterSplit: The pile sorts itself out by student, and anything doubtful is put to you: that step cannot be skipped.
about.afterMarks: The marks in the cells become grades, and the pages land in each student's own work.
about.afterSource: The whole pile stays with the work, next to the per-student pieces in the PDF column. Only you can see it, and the wizard can start from it again without you hunting for the file on disk.

scan.secondReaderOn: Every header is read twice: once by the reader you picked, once by Mathpix. Where the two disagree you will be asked to look at the sheet yourself. It roughly doubles what the pile costs.
scan.secondReaderOff: Every header is read once, names and marks together. Cheaper, but a misread name looks exactly as confident as a correct one.

scan.headerless: No header found here: most likely a question paper.
scan.batchRefused: The run was recorded: the students have their work and their marks. The pile itself could not be kept, though — there was no room for it: either the file is over the limit or the school has used up its storage. Nothing here can start a new run from it, so keep your own copy of the scan.
scan.commonConditionsHint: This sheet comes before the first piece of work and carries no header, so it is the question paper — handed out once for everybody. A run like this marks no boundaries (there is nothing for it to divide) and is not worth reading for marks, but it does go into every student's PDF, at the front: otherwise they open their answers without the questions. If it is somebody's work after all, name the owner below and the sheet stops being shared.

scan.commonConditionsLine_other: {{count}} question sheets lie once at the top of the pile (pages {{pages}}) — they go to the front of every student's work.

{{count}} pages will go, and reading them again costs money: a page is not read twice while it is here.
